It is the 'only standing candidate,' and acting on it is the only rational option in the absence of alternatives, requiring no positive inductive support.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the set of possible theories is infinite, making 'only standing candidate' a meaningless status.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If acting on the survivor implicitly assumes it won't be falsified immediately (a form of induction).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'rational action' requires a positive reason to believe success, not just the absence of known failure.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Eliminative Rationality: Induction requires inferring the truth of a theory from positive instances. Popperian preference infers nothing about the truth of the survivor. It merely notes that Theory A is falsified, Theory B is falsified, and Theory C is not (yet). To act on A or B is irrational (known false). To act on C is the only logical option left. This is a deductive elimination of options, not an inductive promotion of the winner. The 'preference' is simply the recognition of a null set of viable alternatives.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
